## Anovulation Symptoms: 7 Signs You're Not Ovulating

You can have a period every month and still not be ovulating. That surprises most people, and it is the reason anovulation goes undetected for so long.

**Key takeaways**
- Anovulation means no egg is released in a cycle.
- Bleeding can continue, so a regular period does not confirm ovulation.
- The most reliable at-home confirmation is a rise in progesterone (measured as PdG in urine) in the luteal phase.

### What is anovulation?

Anovulation is a menstrual cycle in which the ovary does not release an egg. Most people have an occasional anovulatory cycle. It becomes clinically relevant when it happens repeatedly, because conception is not possible in a cycle without an egg.

### 7 anovulation symptoms

1. **Irregular cycle length** — cycles shorter than 21 days or longer than 35, or varying by more than 7–9 days month to month.
2. **No temperature shift** — basal body temperature stays flat instead of rising after ovulation.
3. **No progesterone (PdG) rise** — the clearest signal, because progesterone only rises after an egg is released.
4. **Absent or unchanging cervical mucus** — no shift to the clear, stretchy mucus that normally appears near ovulation.
5. **Very light or very heavy bleeding** — unopposed estrogen changes the lining, so flow becomes unpredictable.
6. **Persistently negative or continuously positive LH tests** — in [PCOS](https://example.com/blog/pcos), LH can stay elevated without ovulation following.
7. **Missed periods** — the most obvious sign, though the least common of the seven.

### What causes anovulation?

The most common cause is PCOS. Thyroid dysfunction, high prolactin, very low body weight, extended intense exercise, perimenopause, and chronic stress also disrupt the hormonal signal that triggers ovulation. A [2019 review in *Human Reproduction Update*](https://example.org/humupd-review) attributes the majority of anovulatory infertility to PCOS.

### How anovulation is confirmed

| Method | What it measures | Confirms ovulation? |
|---|---|---|
| Calendar tracking | Cycle length only | No |
| LH strips | LH surge before ovulation | No — predicts, doesn't confirm |
| Basal body temperature | Post-ovulation temp shift | Retrospectively |
| PdG (urine progesterone) | Progesterone metabolite after ovulation | Yes |
| Mid-luteal serum progesterone | Blood progesterone | Yes, clinic-based |

### When to see a doctor

See a clinician if you have had no period for 90 days, cycles consistently outside 21–35 days, or have been trying to conceive for 12 months (6 months if over 35).

### FAQ

**Can you have a period without ovulating?** Yes. Anovulatory bleeding is withdrawal bleeding from unopposed estrogen, not a true post-ovulation period.

**Does anovulation mean infertility?** No. It means conception is not possible in that specific cycle. Most causes are treatable.
